title: architecture-review-kv-cache-connections-notes-2026-05-25
content:
Architecture Review: KV Cache Connections and Routing - Meeting notes (2026-05-25)

Attendees:
- Priya Kapoor (owner)
- Ethan Morales
- Lina Zhang
- Marco Rivera
- Samir Patel
- Guests: QA: Tara Nguyen, SRE: Omar El-Sayed

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of RFC-142 (sharding strategy) and RFC-151 (eviction/latency tradeoffs)
2) Present connection model options for KV cache access across multi-route setups
3) Evaluate routing/fallback behavior under contention and partial failures
4) Agree on short-term changes for the next sprint + long-term design decisions

Context / Motivation:
- We continue to see higher tail latency in multi-tenant KV cache lookups when routing across multiple GPU pools and model variant routes.
- Recent load spikes (customer A, May 14) exposed connection pressure between frontends and cache workers; SRE mitigated with rate-limit fallback but user QoE impacted.
- Need an operationally simple connection model that integrates with existing sharding (RFC-142) and eviction policies (RFC-151), while enabling prefetching and per-tenant routing policies.

Notes and Discussion:
1) Connection model options presented (Lina):
   - Option A: Dedicated long-lived connections per route-to-gpu-pool (connection pooling keyed by route+pool). Pros: low dial latency, stable; Cons: higher socket count, more state on frontends.
   - Option B: Shared multiplexed connections to an ingress proxy per region (single connection per region per frontend). Pros: reduced sockets, simplified pooling; Cons: proxy becomes a hotspot and complicates per-route policies.
   - Option C: On-demand ephemeral connections with aggressive caching of channel objects (LRU expiration). Pros: minimal state; Cons: high open/close overhead under bursty workloads.

   Discussion: Team consensus leans to Option A for short term (predictable latency) and Option B as the long-term target once proxy HA is proven. Lina noted Option A meshes well with RFC-142 sharding keys since route+pool maps deterministically to shard owner.

2) Routing & fallback behavior (Priya/Ethan):
   - Decided fallback order for a request: primary route -> preferred variant pool -> regional fallback pool -> degraded CPU-bound path.
   - On connection exhaustion: rather than immediate fail, attempt queued wait with backpressure window (configurable; default 50ms). After window, trigger fallback route. This avoids cascading restarts.
   - For multi-route requests (splitter), prefer sticky connections to the same shard to preserve cache locality; if sticky pool is overloaded, re-evaluate routing policy to switch to warm-pool variant.

3) Eviction and prefetch coordination (Marco):
   - Eviction events (RFC-151) should emit soft hints to orchestrator so prefetch agents can prioritize rehydration for hot prefixes.
   - Prefetch window size and concurrency must be rate-limited to avoid overload. Proposed defaults: 4 concurrent prefetches per route, 100ms inter-prefetch spacing.

4) Observability and tracing (Samir/Tara):
   - Add span tags for: route_id, shard_id, connection_pool_id, prefetch_hint, eviction_reason.
   - Introduce new dashboard: KV-cache connection health (sockets used, wait-time P50/P95/P99, reconnects/sec).

Decisions (agreed):
- Short-term (next sprint): adopt Option A (dedicated long-lived per route+pool connection pools). Rationale: predictable latency and simple mapping to existing shard ownership.
- Medium-term: prototype Option B (region-level multiplexing) behind a HA proxy. Evaluate at 2x load in staging before any production migrations.
- Backpressure policy: implement queued wait window 50ms default, configurable per-route, then failover to fallback route.
- Sticky-connection policy for multi-route requests to preserve cache locality; provide opt-out flag for splitters.
- Prefetch coordination: integrate eviction signals with prefetcher; use conservative defaults (4 concurrent per route).
- Observability: add the specified span tags and the KV-cache connection health dashboard.

Action Items / Owners / Due dates:
- Lina: Implement connection pool prototype (route+pool key) in serving-runtime; include metrics hooks. Due 2026-06-08.
- Marco: Add prefetch rate-limiting and eviction hooks in prefetcher service. Due 2026-06-10.
- Samir: Create dashboard wireframe and tracing spec PR; include example spans. Due 2026-06-03.
- Ethan: Update routing policy config schema to support backpressure window and fallback order; file RFC patch. Due 2026-06-01.
- Priya: Coordinate on staging experiment plan for Option B proxy; draft test matrix and SLA checks. Due 2026-06-15.
- QA (Tara): Add regression tests covering connection exhaustion and fallback behavior. Due 2026-06-12.

Open Questions / Risks:
- Socket limits on frontends at scale: we need SRE to confirm safe per-host open file/socket limits for Option A at 500k concurrent connections scenario. (Omar to follow up).
- Impact on autoscaling: sticky-connection policies can increase tail imbalance; autoscaler polarity needs to consider connection pressure signals.
- Cost of persistent connections for Dedicated customers with many reserved pools - billing/chargeback implications. Finance/product review recommended.

Follow-ups / Next meeting:
- Weekly sync to track action items; invite SRE to confirm socket limits.
- Tentative follow-up deep-dive on Option B proxy design: 2026-06-09.

Appendix / References:
- RFC-142: KV cache sharding (existing)
- RFC-151: Eviction latency tradeoffs
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 (connection-pool-prototype)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-7823 (investigate multi-route tail latencies)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working note aimed at capturing decisions and immediate action items. Please comment on the queued wait window default and prefetch concurrency if you have workload-specific concerns.
- If ok, Lina will open a WIP PR with the connection pool code and basic benchmarks; link will be added to linked_artifacts.
